attempts.validity: blockers COMPLETE, other edges 1, pool timeouts 304

A.rule: a non-ledger_app session blocked ledger_app sessions in 53 samples; 304 pool acquisition timeouts

report.summary: A restart at 18:52:34 shrank the DB pool from 10 to 1 connection with a 250 ms timeout. With an idle-in-transaction session blocking a query, transfers hit pool acquisition timeouts and returned 500/503.

findings.claim: Config changed at the 18:52:34 restart: poolMaximumSize 10->1 and connection timeout 30000->250 ms.
findings.reason: Runtime config shows the change and a restart inside the window.

findings.claim: The 1-connection pool was exhausted: 304 acquisition timeouts, pending borrowers up to 2 (18:52:53-18:54:38).
findings.reason: Pool metrics show timeouts and pending borrowers while the maximum was 1.

findings.claim: Transfers failed (40% 5xx, p95 1.7 s) because of pool starvation; an idle-in-transaction session blocking a ledger_app session (18:52:36-18:54:40) worsened it.
findings.reason: Errors and latency coincide with the pool timeouts; the blocker held the single connection longer. The link to the 5xx is not directly traced.

findings.claim: Outbox arrivals and publications dropped to near zero after the restart, then recovered. Deliveries succeeded (365/365, ~71 ms).
findings.reason: Delivery to the consumer was healthy; the throughput dip tracks the commit failures, not the consumer.

limitations: Scrape gap 18:52:28-18:52:38 and a counter restart limit the metrics; 43 gauge samples were NaN, probably during pool exhaustion.
The owner or origin of the idle-in-transaction session, and the reason for the config change, are not shown.
